column1: # WPT area refusals: area<TAB>ADR/reason<TAB>full|partial<TAB>what is refused
# Each row maps a WPT area (as it appears in directories.txt and wpt-baseline.md)
# to the ADR that says this browser will not implement the capability it tests.
# Only areas in our directories.txt checkout are listed here. Areas not checked
# out (webrtc/, geolocation/, webaudio/, etc.) are implicitly refused by their
# absence from directories.txt.
# The third column is load-bearing and was the reason this file sat empty until
# 2026-08-17: every refusal here is *partial*, and a reader that treated a
# partial refusal as a full one would tell an agent to stop working an area
# where most of the tests are ordinary bugs. `full` means do not chase the area
# at all; `partial` means some named failures in it are deliberate, and the
# area's ceiling is Firefox's rate on the tests this browser can run.
# A refusal is a decision with a name, not a bug. When a test fails because of
# one, the expectation line carries a comment naming the ADR -- rule 1 of
# docs/wpt-plan.md §0, not a new rule.
# --- Full refusals: the entire area is out of scope ---
# (none of the checked-out areas are fully refused; areas like webrtc/ and
# geolocation/ are not in directories.txt at all)
# --- Partial refusals ---
